# Disagreement Log — 1 Kings Chapter 16
**Reviewed by:** SOPHIA | **Date:** 2026-03-11

---

## Summary
22 verse(s) flagged for significant translation divergence.

### Verse 4
**EMET (literal):** The-one-belonging-to-Baasha who-dies in-the-city, the-dogs will-eat, and-the-one-belonging-to-him who-dies in-the-field, the-birds-of the-heavens will-eat."

**LOGOS (formal):** Anyone belonging to Baasha who dies in the city the dogs shall eat, and anyone of his who dies in the field the birds of the heavens shall eat."

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Dogs will eat any of Baasha's family who die in the city, and vultures will eat any who die in the countryside."

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 5
**EMET (literal):** And-the-rest-of the-acts-of Baasha and-what he-did and-his-might — are-they not written in-the-Book-of the-Chronicles-of the-Kings-of Israel?

**LOGOS (formal):** Now the rest of the acts of Baasha and what he did, and his might, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** The rest of Baasha's reign — what he did and his military accomplishments — is recorded in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 6
**EMET (literal):** And-Baasha lay-down with his-fathers and-was-buried in-Tirzah. And-Elah his-son reigned in-his-place.

**LOGOS (formal):** And Baasha slept with his fathers and was buried at Tirzah, and Elah his son reigned in his place.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Baasha died and was buried in Tirzah. His son Elah succeeded him.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 7
**EMET (literal):** And-also by-the-hand-of Jehu son-of Hanani the-prophet, the-word-of YHWH came against Baasha and-against his-house — both because-of all the-evil that he-did in-the-eyes-of YHWH, to-provoke-him with-the-work-of his-hands, to-be like the-house-of Jeroboam, and-also because he-struck-it.

**LOGOS (formal):** Moreover, the word of the LORD came by the prophet Jehu the son of Hanani against Baasha and his house, both because of all the evil that he did in the sight of the LORD, provoking him to anger with the work of his hands, in being like the house of Jeroboam, and also because he destroyed it.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** The LORD's message through the prophet Jehu son of Hanani was directed against Baasha and his house both because of all the evil he had done in the LORD's sight, provoking him with his actions (just like the house of Jeroboam), and because he had destroyed it.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 9
**EMET (literal):** And-his-servant Zimri, commander-of half the-chariots, conspired against-him. And-he was in-Tirzah, drinking-himself-drunk in-the-house-of Arza, who was over the-house in-Tirzah.

**LOGOS (formal):** But his servant Zimri, commander of half his chariots, conspired against him. When he was at Tirzah, drinking himself drunk in the house of Arza, who was over the household in Tirzah,

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** His officer Zimri, commander of half the chariot force, plotted against him. While Elah was in Tirzah, getting drunk at the home of Arza, his palace manager,

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 11
**EMET (literal):** And-it-was when-he-became-king, when-he-sat on his-throne, he-struck ʾet-all the-house-of Baasha. He-did-not leave to-him one-who-urinates-against-a-wall, nor-his-kinsman, nor-his-friend.

**LOGOS (formal):** When he began to reign, as soon as he had seated himself on his throne, he struck down all the house of Baasha. He did not leave him a single male, neither of his kinsmen nor of his friends.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** As soon as he was seated on the throne, he killed off Baasha's entire family. He didn't spare a single male — relative or friend.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 12
**EMET (literal):** And-Zimri destroyed ʾet-all the-house-of Baasha, according-to-the-word-of YHWH that he-spoke against Baasha by-the-hand-of Jehu the-prophet —

**LOGOS (formal):** Thus Zimri destroyed all the house of Baasha, according to the word of the LORD, which he spoke against Baasha by Jehu the prophet,

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Zimri wiped out the entire house of Baasha, just as the LORD had declared through the prophet Jehu —

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 14
**EMET (literal):** And-the-rest-of the-acts-of Elah and-all that he-did — are-they not written in-the-Book-of the-Chronicles-of the-Kings-of Israel?

**LOGOS (formal):** Now the rest of the acts of Elah and all that he did, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** The rest of Elah's reign and everything he did are recorded in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 15
**EMET (literal):** In-the-twenty-seventh year-of Asa king-of Judah, Zimri reigned seven days in-Tirzah. And-the-people were-encamped against Gibbethon, that belonged-to the-Philistines.

**LOGOS (formal):** In the twenty-seventh year of Asa king of Judah, Zimri reigned seven days in Tirzah. Now the troops were encamped against Gibbethon, which belonged to the Philistines,

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** In the twenty-seventh year of King Asa of Judah, Zimri reigned in Tirzah — for seven days. The Israelite army was besieging the Philistine town of Gibbethon at the time.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 16
**EMET (literal):** And-the-people who-were-encamped heard, saying, "Zimri has-conspired and-also has-struck the-king." And-all Israel made ʾet-Omri, commander-of the-army, king over Israel on-that day in-the-camp.

**LOGOS (formal):** and the troops who were encamped heard it said, "Zimri has conspired, and he has also struck down the king." Therefore all Israel made Omri, the commander of the army, king over Israel that day in the camp.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** When the troops in the field heard that Zimri had conspired and assassinated the king, they proclaimed Omri, the army commander, king of Israel right there in the camp.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

— SOPHIA
